# 1 Enoch Chapter 36 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 36 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 36:3 — "the path which is shown to them" vs. "the paths that have been laid out for them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the path which is shown to them" | Literal; singular "path" |
| LOGOS | "the path that is shown to them" | Same; relative pronoun updated |
| PNEUMA | "the paths that have been laid out for them" | Plural "paths"; "laid out" for "shown" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the path that is shown to them." The Ge'ez uses a singular: the stars follow a single westward path shown to them, not individual paths. "Shown" preserves the divine guidance element (God shows the stars their way); PNEUMA's "laid out" loses this relational nuance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 36:4 — the closing doxology structure

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I blessed always the Lord of Glory...to show the greatness of his work to the angels and to human beings, that these might praise his work and all his creatures: that they might see the work of his power and praise the great work of his hands and bless him for ever" | Literal; complex relative clauses |
| LOGOS | "I always blessed the Lord of Glory...to show the greatness of his work to the angels and to human beings, that they might praise his work and all his creatures: that they might see the work of his power and praise the great work of his hands and bless him forever" | Formal; "that they" for "that these" |
| PNEUMA | "I praised the Lord of Glory...because he chose to show the greatness of his work...so that they would worship what he has made...so that they would see his mighty power at work and celebrate the great deeds of his hands and bless him forever" | Dynamic paraphrase; "because he chose" restructures causality |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The doxology's purpose clauses ("that they might...") preserves the consecutive Ge'ez infinitive-purpose structure. EMET's "these" is an archaic demonstrative pronoun; LOGOS's "they" is correct. PNEUMA's "because he chose" inserts an unwarranted agential interpretation, and "worship what he has made" substitutes a generic worship term for the specific "praise his work."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 36:4 — "great and glorious wonders" vs. "great and glorious wonders"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "great and glorious wonders" | Literal pair |
| LOGOS | "great and glorious wonders" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "such great and wondrous deeds" | "Wondrous deeds" for "wonders"; "such" adds emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "great and glorious wonders." The Ge'ez uses the specific term "glorious" (sebt) which PNEUMA drops in favor of "wondrous deeds." "Wonders" is the correct noun form; "deeds" is an interpretation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---
